title: Policy Loom: adaptive throttle autoscaler for throughput guarantees
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce 'Policy Loom', a new autoscaling policy engine component designed to deliver per-tenant throughput guarantees while protecting fleet stability and cost. This ticket covers the algorithm design, target metric selection, safety fences (surge caps, cooldowns, rollback triggers), and a pragmatic implementation that can operate alongside existing headroom controllers. The engine will (1) synthesize short-window percentile latency, sustained token/sec demand, and tokenized request concurrency into a single target throughput signal, (2) use a blended controller combining a conservative PI loop with quantile-based demand spikes detector, and (3) enforce safety limits (max surge, warmup lanes, KV-affinity preservation) to avoid cross-tenant interference.
acceptance_criteria: Policy Loom exposes a documented policy proto and REST API for per-tenant target throughput and safety parameters
On synthetic workload tests, configured tenant guarantees are met within 1.5x of target with <5% SLA violations for steady-state demand
Safety limits prevent more than configured surge (default 2x committed throughput) and obey cooldown windows during repeated spikes
Canary rollout shows no regression in global latency P95 or per-tenant cost beyond agreed thresholds
Unit/integration tests for controller logic and a reproducible load test harness are checked in and green
design_notes: High-level decisions: (A) Target metrics: we will compute a blended target signal made from 3 inputs: short-window p50/p90 latency (to protect latency-sensitive paths), token/sec demand (30s window EWMA), and a sustained concurrency signal (KV-cache hit-aware). (B) Controller: base controller = PI with adaptive gain limited by headroom credits; overlay spike detector triggers temporary conservative surge with precise TTL. (C) Safety fences: max_surge_ratio, min_sustain_seconds, cooldown_window_seconds, and rollback_trigger_fraction. (D) Placement: Policy Loom will expose per-tenant policy objects stored in config DB and executed in the autoscaler control-plane; enforcement occurs by emitting desired fleet allocation intents rather than immediate slot changes to allow downstream orchestrator to respect scheduling constraints. Trade-offs: PI gives stability but slow reaction; so we add a quantile spike layer to catch tail-fan-out events. We prefer conservative defaults to prioritize reliability over cost in initial rollout. Metrics for monitoring: desired_vs_actual_throughput, headroom_credits, surge_count, enforced_cooldowns, policy_evaluations/sec.
implementation_plan: Define policy proto and defaults (max_surge_ratio, cooldown_window, warmup_allocation) - 2d
Implement blended target signal module and unit tests - 4d
Implement controller with safe clamps and headroom credits integration - 5d
Integrate with existing allocation reconciler (emit intents) and add feature flags - 3d
Add telemetry (metrics, traces, dashboards) and synthetic load harness - 4d
Run staging canary and iterate on tuning - 3d
testing_plan: Unit tests covering controller gains, clamp edge cases and spike detector behavior
Integration tests in CI that run the allocation reconciler with a simulated cluster (deterministic workload traces)
Load tests in staging using tokenized request generator with mixed tail/steady workloads
Chaos test: schedule transient node loss during a high-surge scenario to validate graceful degradation
Canary in production on 3 low-risk tenants with close monitoring for 48h
rollout_plan: Canary to 3 tenants (low to medium traffic) for 48h
If canary stable, broaden to 10% of capacity for 72h while monitoring key metrics
Full rollout by toggling feature flag after stakeholder sign-off
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and automated regression alerts
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive surge could evict KV cache and increase tail latency. Mitigation: affinity-aware allocation and warmup lanes reserved during surge
Risk: overfitting to synthetic traces causing oscillation in real traffic. Mitigation: conservative default PID gains and staged tuning with production traces
Risk: cost blowout if many tenants trigger surge simultaneously. Mitigation: global surge budget and per-tenant max_surge_ratio plus prioritized shedding policies
Risk: policy config errors cause unexpected scaling. Mitigation: schema validation, dry-run mode, and a safe default that denies surges unless explicitly allowed
